prerequisites: Mathematics, especially complex numbers, vectors, solving systems of equations, and differential and integral calculus.
Recommended English language proficiency to understand bibliography.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.

teaching_methods: Lectures, introducing theory and solving exercises on the board.
Interactive classes for solving proposed problems.
Problem solving by students, including exercises at the end of each topic.
Laboratory practicals (4 sessions in small groups, with theoretical explanations of equipment, group work, and software simulations).

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practical attendance, report, and pre-lab quizzes

assessment_rules: Exams will be conducted in person, with a minimum grade of 5/10 required in each of the three exams to pass the course. Attendance at practicals is compulsory to pass the course, and its 10% weight is not re-evaluable. The extraordinary exam will have the same structure as the ordinary exams (practical exam, first and second partials). Previously passed partials or practicals exempt students from repeating those parts in the extraordinary exam. The minimum grade requirement for each test is maintained.
